title: Say or tell, make or do
goal: Choose between words that Indian speakers often mix up
intro: Some pairs of words look similar but are used differently: say and tell, speak and talk, borrow and lend, bring and take, make and do, lose and miss. Knowing the pattern for each pair makes your English sound much more natural.

rules.rule: borrow FROM someone; lend TO someone.
examples: Can you lend me your pen?

rules.rule: make = create or produce; do = work, tasks, activities.
examples: make a cake, make a mistake, make a decision
do homework, do the dishes, do a favour

rules.rule: bring = to here; take = to there.
examples: Bring your laptop to my desk.
Take this file to the manager.

mistakes.wrong: Can you borrow me your book?
mistakes.right: Can you lend me your book?

mistakes.wrong: He told that he was busy.
mistakes.right: He said that he was busy.

mistakes.why: lose = can’t find; miss = didn’t catch or feel sad without.

ex.q: Could you ___ me some money until Monday?
I need to ___ a decision soon.
Can I lend your charger for a minute?
ex.fixed: Can I borrow your charger for a minute?

ex.q: He said me to wait outside.
ex.fixed: He told me to wait outside.

ex.q: Can you do me a ___? (favour / help)

ex.a: Please take these books back to the library.

ex.q: Correct this: “Can you borrow me your bike?”
a: Can you lend me your bike
ex.y: Can you lend me… / Can I borrow…

talk: Tell the coach about a time you borrowed or lent something, a mistake you made, and something someone told you that you still remember.
